provider.description: What serves it: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or your own signed-in Claude Code CLI on your Claude subscription (docs/04 The Claude Code provider; never an API key).

endpoint.description: An OpenAI-compatible base URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 (llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama's /v1), or https:// (the server's certificate checked against the system's roots). Not for claude-code.

model.description: The model id a request names; the profile's name when unset. For claude-code: opus, sonnet, haiku, fable or a full id; default: the CLI's. Which Claude model a turn uses as the plan runs ahead of pace is a group's chain (ai.groups, docs/04 Pacing).

pacing.description: Gone with model auto (the first pacing design): the server moves it into ai.groups once, as paced places of each role that named the profile (docs/04 Pacing).

target.description: session: spend each 5-hour window fully; week: stretch the weekly limit across the week; both: the stricter of the two.

contextWindow.description: Tokens; 0 when unknown (a context error reveals it).

maxOutput.description: Tokens a reply may take; 0 leaves it to the server.

vision.description: Whether the images tool results show are sent to it (a vision model; llama.cpp with its projector). Left out: what its server says (llama.cpp's /props modalities, asked once per server run); Test connection shows it.

keepThinking.description: A llama.cpp server is sent the turn's earlier thinking with each step (reasoning_content), as its chat template expects; false sends only the replies.

effort.description: What each effort adds to a request: the fields written into it, e.g. {"low": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}}. A level left out adds nothing. Left out: a llama.cpp server is sent chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort, any other server reasoning_effort (docs/04 Model groups and roles).

env.description: The environment variable that holds the key. Keys never live in settings files.

prefillRate.description: Prompt tokens per second assumed until one is measured (default 150).

pace.description: A Claude model's place is used while the plan's pace against target is at most max; over it, a turn goes on down the chain (docs/04 Pacing). Left out: always.

max.description: 1.0 runs out exactly at the reset; 1.25 spends a quarter faster.

target.description: session: spend each 5-hour window fully; week: stretch the weekly limit across the week; both: the stricter of the two.

fallback.description: Tried in order after the role's model: a model's name, or {model, pace} for a Claude model used only while on pace.

agent.description: A sub-agent of the group (docs/04 A group is a topology): a role, what it is for, the mode its chat runs in and the agents it may run itself.

description.description: What the orchestrator is told it is for.

calls.description: The agents it may run itself; ["*"] every one; none by default.

group.description: An orchestrator - primary, with planning and implementation for Plan and Agent mode - and its sub-agents.

ai.models.description: Model profiles by name: where each model is served and how to talk to it (docs/04 Providers).

ai.groups.description: Model groups by name, each a topology: an orchestrator - per role (primary, planning, implementation) a model, temperature, effort and fallbacks; a Claude model in a chain may have a pace; a chat's mode picks the role: Ask primary, Plan planning, Agent implementation, a role left off is primary - and its sub-agents, agents, which the orchestrator runs with agent_run (docs/04 Model groups, A group is a topology, Pacing).

ai.defaultGroup.description: The group a new chat uses; empty: the first group.

ai.permissions.description: Rules for the AI's tool calls (docs/11): deny, then confirm (always ask), then the chat's permission mode, then allow. A rule is kind(pattern): shell(nuke build *), fs.write(src/**), fs.*(secrets/**).

ai.resumeInterrupted.description: A turn a server restart cut off: agent - an Agent-mode chat goes on by itself once IED is back (at most 3 restarts in a row; others wait for your next message); always - every chat does; never - every chat waits for you (docs/12 Restart behavior). A chat whose tool restarted IED on purpose (ied_relaunch) always goes on.

ai.maxSteps.description: Model requests one turn may make before it pauses; 0 is no limit (docs/12 Budgets). Loop and no-progress detection still pause a turn that runs away.

ai.chats.keepDeletedDays.description: Days a deleted chat is kept, whole and restorable from the Chats list's Deleted section, before it is removed for good (docs/04 Deleting a chat).

ai.chats.notify.description: Telling you when a chat's turn ends or waits for you (an approval, a question) in a window that is not showing that chat: all - a toast, and a system notification while the window is in the background (the browser asks once whether IED may show them); toasts - only the toast; off - neither. Clicking either opens the chat there, the desktop app's window brought to the front (docs/15 Chat).

ai.chats.panelRows.description: Rows a long list of a chat's details panel shows - modified files, tasks, background tasks, the clipboard, what the chat has open - before its Show all (docs/15 Chat).

ai.claude.command.description: The Claude Code CLI's program and leading arguments. Empty: claude.exe on PATH, then the native installer's (%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin), WinGet's link, then the newest the Claude desktop app keeps (the app from Anthropic's installer or the Microsoft Store). Sign in to it with your Claude subscription (Settings > AI > Claude > Sign in, or claude auth login in a terminal of your own): IED never handles Claude credentials and never runs Claude on an API key.

ai.claude.usageRefreshMinutes.description: How often the plan's usage (the 5-hour session and the week) is asked of the CLI while a claude-code model is set up; 0: only when asked and after Claude turns. Asking spends no usage.

ai.edits.formatOnWrite.description: Format a file the AI writes (fs_write, fs_edit) with its language server before the call returns, where the language's plugin asks for it (its language server profile's formatOnAiWrite). The result says what formatting changed (docs/24 After an AI edit).

ai.edits.diagnosticsOnWrite.description: Give the AI what the language server says of a file it just wrote - its errors and warnings, and the other files it finds problems in - where the language's plugin asks for it (diagnosticsOnAiWrite). Information only: a write with errors still succeeds, since files mid-way through an edit of several are expected to break (docs/24 After an AI edit).

ai.edits.diagnosticsWaitMs.description: How long an AI write waits for the language server's diagnostics of the file (and for a starting server) before it returns without them; problems_list has them later.

ai.claude.paceDays.description: What a weekly window's pace counts (docs/04 Pacing): week - all seven days; workweek - only the work days (ai.claude.workDays), midnight to midnight in the time zone of the computer IED runs on, so a weekend does not count and the pace stands still through it. The bars still show the whole week, with a mark where the even line stands through each weekend. The 5-hour session counts every hour either way.

ai.claude.workDays.description: The work days a weekly window's pace counts when ai.claude.paceDays is workweek; none named: every day.

ai.tools.loadAll.description: Send every tool's definition with every request. Off, plugin tools and tool groups are listed by name and loaded on demand with tool_search, which keeps the context small (docs/13 Loading tools on demand).
